tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

details.reference: USP Description and Relative Solubility; USP2024 Monograph for Inositol

tests.procedure: Stepwise solubility (USP descriptive terms): 100 mg sample in a stoppered tube with 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min (repeat once if not dissolved); add 0.9 mL, then 2 mL, then 7 mL solvent with the same shake and hold to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved, 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble), then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with the other solvents.

Clarity of solution: sample solution 100 mg/mL in colourless neutral glass tubes, compared with reference suspensions A and B and water in diffused daylight, viewed vertically against a black background; sample must show the same clarity as water. Colour of solution: the sample solution (from the clarity test) is compared with standard solutions A, B and C and water in diffused daylight, viewed vertically against a white background; sample must not be more intensely coloured than any of them.

details.clarityReferences: reference suspensions A (5.0 mL of opalescence standard to 100 mL) and B (10.0 mL to 100 mL), and water

colourStandards.A: 2.5 mL standard stock A (2.4 mL ferric chloride CS, 0.6 mL cobaltous chloride CS, 7.0 mL diluted HCl) to 100 mL
colourStandards.B: 2.5 mL standard stock B (2.4 mL ferric chloride CS, 1.0 mL cobaltous chloride CS, 0.4 mL cupric sulfate CS, 6.2 mL diluted HCl) to 100 mL
colourStandards.C: 0.75 mL standard stock C (9.6 mL ferric chloride CS, 0.2 mL cobaltous chloride CS, 0.2 mL cupric sulfate CS) to 100 mL

tests.procedure: IR identification: mix sample intimately with potassium bromide, compress into a transparent pellet, examine the spectrum and compare with that of Inositol RS.

tests.procedure: Barium: to 10 mL of the sample solution (from the clarity test, 100 mg/mL) add 1 mL diluted sulfuric acid; read immediately and after 1 h. Opalescence must not be more intense than a mixture of 1 mL water and 10 mL sample solution.

Limit of lead by AAS (USP <852>): dissolve 20.0 g inositol in diluted acetic acid and make up to 100 mL; add 2.0 mL saturated ammonium pyrrolidinedithiocarbamate and 10.0 mL methyl isobutyl ketone, shake 30 s, protect from bright light, separate, use the MIBK layer. Standards: 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 mL of standard lead solution (10 µg Pb/mL) added to 20.0 g inositol and treated the same way. Blank: as sample without inositol. Atomic absorption, 283.3 nm, lead hollow-cathode lamp, air-acetylene flame; zero on blank, read sample and the three standards; limit NMT 0.5 mg/kg.

details.standardLeadSolution: 10 µg Pb per mL (lead nitrate stock 159.8 mg in 1000 mL water with 1 mL nitric acid, 10.0 mL to 100.0 mL on the day of use)

tests.procedure: Organic impurities (USP, HPLC RI): use the assay mobile phase, sample solution and standard solution as in the assay; dilute 2.0 mL of the assay standard solution to 100 mL with water as the impurity standard; injection volume 20 µL. Impurity (%) = (rU/rS) x (CS/CU) x 100.

details.standardSolution: 50 mg/mL USP Inositol RS (assay standard solution)
details.impurityStandard: 2.0 mL of the assay standard solution to 100 mL with water
details.reference: USP 2024 <621> Chromatography; USP2024 Monograph for Inositol

tests.procedure: Conductivity: sample solution 0.2 g/mL inositol in purified water; rinse the calibrated conductivity cell with boiled and cooled water and twice with the sample solution; measure while gently stirring with a magnetic stirrer.
Water determination (Karl Fischer, USP <921>) on a 1.0 g sample with a calibrated Karl Fischer apparatus.

Assay (USP, HPLC refractive index): mobile phase water; system suitability solution 0.05 mg/mL USP Inositol RS and 0.05 mg/mL USP Mannitol RS; standard solution 50 mg/mL USP Inositol RS; sample solution 50 mg/mL inositol. Column 7.8-mm x 30-cm, packing L19, 85 °C; RI detector at a constant 30-35 °C; flow 0.5 mL/min; injection 10 µL. Relative retention: inositol 1.0, mannitol 1.3. Result (%) = (rU/rS) x (CS/CU) x 100, on the anhydrous basis.
